A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLBR framework and Reward Bag Transformer. All 20 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo experiments, reward-bag comparisons, component ablations and a Hopper reward-reconstruction case study, including additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds DeepMind Control Suite results, reward-shaping comparisons and architecture-sensitivity experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The specified architecture receives limited revisions: v2 reports three causal Transformer layers instead of one and omits the separate post-attention reward linear decoder described and depicted in v1. Bidirectional attention was already present; the redistribution equation, dual losses and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 adds cheetah-run, quadruped-walk, fish-upright and cartpole-swingup from the DeepMind Control Suite to the four retained MuJoCo tasks. This substantially broadens evaluated control tasks, including upright stabilization and swing-up, under fixed-length bags and trajectory feedback.

E2.justification: Appendix D.4 and Figure 6 add SAC-shaping, following Hu et al. (2020), to the Hopper-v2 and Walker2d-v2 comparisons. SAC, IRCR, RRD, LIRPG and HC remain. The expanded discussion of excluding RUDDER and Align-RUDDER does not establish removal of previously reported comparators.

E3.justification: Table 2 and the implementation appendix revise causal Transformer depth from one to three layers, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. The new Ant-v2 sensitivity study crosses training lengths 100/200/500 with relabeling lengths 25/50/100. Existing episode horizons, training budgets and bag-length settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds two diagnostic investigations: sensitivity to training and relabeling windows in Appendix D.5, and whether conventional reward shaping helps across bag lengths in Appendix D.4. The existing component ablation and detailed Hopper case study are retained in D.2 and D.3, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report six-seed means and standard deviations for principal comparisons and ablations, three trials for Table 3, and paired t-tests at 5% for Tables 1 and 3. The added studies use existing three- or six-run reporting practices; no increased repeat count or new statistical procedure is established.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds results across four DeepMind Control tasks and seven feedback settings. Figures 6 and 9 add shaping and sensitivity results, including better SAC-shaping performance than SAC at longer bags and dependence on sequence/relabeling lengths. Tables 1 and 3 retain every numerical entry, and the original Hopper case evidence is reused.

T1.justification: The BRMDP definition, bagged-return objective, optimal-policy equivalence theorem and complete proof are retained. The proof moves from Appendix A to B; clearer trajectory-return wording and notation changes introduce no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: v2's abstract replaces the categorical assertion that existing approaches cannot address the setting with comparative superiority, and explicitly foregrounds increasing difficulty with bag length. The introduction adds a potential annotation-effort benefit. The central RLBR, policy-equivalence, RBT and reward-reconstruction contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes LIRPG's weakness to its Markovian sparse-reward setting rather than its on-policy character. It adds interpretations of shaping and architecture sensitivity, explains the annotation-effort versus information-granularity tradeoff, and replaces the sparse-reward future direction with discussion of the current sum-aggregation boundary and possible non-sum extensions.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds the MuJoCo version, reported GPU memory, baseline implementation sources and code/license information. New sequence-length documentation is inconsistent: D.5 and Figure 9's highlighted panel specify training/relabeling lengths 500/100, while its caption states 100/500. The anonymous project-code link is retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against sparse-reward RL through a dedicated related-work discussion covering shaping, curiosity and curricula. It adds non-Markovian-reward and bidirectional-attention references, including Early, Gaon and Brafman, Seo and Devlin. This develops the distinction between bagged feedback and sparse instance-level rewards beyond v1's trajectory-feedback emphasis.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, and the abstract, introduction, related work and method explanation are extensively rewritten. Learning objectives become Section 4.3; the ablation and detailed case discussion move into a reorganized experimental appendix. A broader-impact appendix is added.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the driving illustration, adds a reward-setting schematic, revises the architecture diagram and expands the main performance figure to two rows. It adds shaping and sensitivity figures, relocates the ablation and detailed case figure, and separately redisplays the case's reward plot in the main text.

improvement.justification: The broader control-task evidence and new shaping and sensitivity checks strengthen conclusions already supported in v1. Clearer differentiation from sparse rewards and discussion of non-sum aggregation improve explanation and scope qualification. These gains are tempered by Figure 9's reversed settings and the unexplained depth revision alongside retained results, which leave reproducibility questions.
